TZ-U01: compose(double,increment)(3) applies increment then double and returns8. pipe(3,double,increment) sends3 through double then increment and returns7. Their listed functions run in opposite composition directions.
TZ-C01: Curried map is still lazy: the double call log is empty until consumed. partition_all produces (2,4),(6,8),(10,), preserving the final order; ordinary partition drops that incomplete tail. Use partition_all for no record loss and fresh sources for independent comparisons.
TZ-U02: Default memoization cannot hash the list input and rejects it before price runs. The custom key receives an args tuple and kwargs dict. Normalize items to a tuple and represent discount consistently for keyword/positional calls: discount1 returns5 and its repeated equivalent is a cache hit, while discount2 returns4 through a second actual calculation.
TZ-C02: The external-price example yields4,4,6. Changing price alone does not invalidate the cached qty result; clearing the explicitly supplied cache dictionary allows recomputation. Make the pricing input/version explicit in a pure function or deliberately scope/clear that cache. Do not invent automatic TTL/current-price detection or a returned-function cache_clear method.
TZ-U03: Toolz groupby consumes the whole input immediately and groups the nonconsecutive east records together, giving east=[qty1,qty3],west=[qty2] in record order. It returns retained lists and differs from itertools consecutive-run grouping.
TZ-C03: Use existing reduceby with region key, qty accumulator and init0 to produce east4,west2 without storing lists of every original order. State still grows with distinct region keys and accumulator size; an unbounded key universe needs a deliberate window/eviction or external aggregation policy. This is not constant memory for arbitrary cardinality.
TZ-U04: merge creates a new outer dictionary and later theme=dark wins, while base.theme stays light. It is shallow: options is the same nested object, so appending b through the result also changes base labels to[a,b]. Do not call it a deep immutable copy or conflate later nested edits with the merge call mutating base.theme.
TZ-C04: merge overwrites A with the later5, producing A5,B3,C7. merge_with(sum) receives all same-key values and produces A7,B3,C7, leaving both source billing dictionaries unchanged. Choose the latter for additive charges rather than changing the business rule to last-write replacement.
